kill "$srv" 2>/dev/null; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null
"$PY" "$H" verify relay-reply 6700

cases.purpose: With proxy-dhcp on the server binds UDP 4011 and answers offer-only PXE replies to the source address and port (r4).
cases.oracle: RFC 2131 message layout decoded by an independent Python codec over frames sniffed on the peer side of a veth pair; the peer sends the DHCP messages the scenario names and checks the server replies and lease/hook files.
cases.comparison: Candidate dhcpd serve/run in a mapped user namespace on a veth pair; the independent Python peer in a second network namespace is the DHCP client or relay. Failing assertions print one line each and the summary line must report failed=0.

files.case.sh:
IP=/usr/bin/ip
PY=/usr/bin/python3
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dhcpd.py
die() { echo "SETUP-FAILED $*"; exit 90; }
settle() { read -t "$1" -u 7 line; }
/usr/bin/mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys || die sysfs
$IP link set lo up || die lo
$IP link add veth0 address 02:00:00:00:0a:01 type veth peer name veth1 address 02:00:00:00:0a:02 || die veth
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter || die rpf-all
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/veth0/rp_filter || die rpf-veth0
exec 7<>sync.fifo
exec 8<>go.fifo
$IP addr add 192.0.2.1/24 dev veth0 || die addr
$IP link set veth0 up || die up
dhcpd serve -c server.conf -l leases -i veth0 > serve.out 2> serve.err &
srv=$!
settle 0.3
"$PY" "$H" peer proxy sync.fifo go.fifo  2> peer.err &
peer=$!
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-pid
[[ $line == "pid=$peer" ]] || die "peer-pid-$line"
$IP link set veth1 netns "$peer" || die move
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-ready
[[ $line == ready ]] || die "peer-$line"
echo go >&8
read -t 40 -u 7 line || die peer-done
[[ $line == done ]] || die "peer-$line"
kill "$srv" 2>/dev/null; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null
"$PY" "$H" verify proxy
files.server.conf:

proxy-dhcp on
next-server 192.0.2.1
bootfile pxelinux.0
tftp-server tftp.lab.test
dns 192.0.2.53

cases.purpose: With pxe-vendor-match on, a request without option 60 or with a non-PXE vendor class gets no next-server siaddr, options 66/67/43 or BOOTP file; a PXEClient request does (r5).
cases.oracle: PXE gating semantics from the configuration documentation (options gated by option 60 PXEClient when pxe-vendor-match is on); BOOTP/DHCP field offsets from RFC 2131 decoded by an independent Python codec.
cases.comparison: Offline respond over three requests (no vendor, MSFT 5.0, PXEClient) against a PXE configuration; the independent decoder checks siaddr, options 66/67/43 and the BOOTP file field.

cases.script:
for n in none msft pxe; do dhcpd respond "$(< req-$n.hex)" -c pxe.conf -l leases-$n > reply-$n.hex 2> err-$n.txt; echo "respond-$n-rc=$?"; done
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dhcpd.py verify pxe-gating
cases.stdout:
respond-none-rc=0
respond-msft-rc=0
respond-pxe-rc=0
verified pxe-gating failed=0

cases.purpose: serve --once with no traffic returns status 0 after one idle one-second wait (r6).
cases.oracle: Documented bounded behavior (--once counts an idle one-second select as the iteration), measured with the shell EPOCHREALTIME clock around the call.
cases.comparison: Single candidate invocation inside a mapped user namespace on loopback with an unprivileged server port; elapsed wall time is bracketed between 0.8 s and 2.5 s.

files.case.sh:
export BASHDHCPD_SERVER_PORT=6700
start=$EPOCHREALTIME
dhcpd serve --once -c server.conf -l leases > serve.out 2> serve.err
rc=$?
end=$EPOCHREALTIME
ms=$(( (${end/./} - ${start/./}) / 1000 ))
echo "serve-rc=$rc"
echo "returned-after-one-idle-second=$([[ $ms -ge 800 && $ms -le 2500 ]] && echo yes || echo "no-${ms}ms")"
